-------------------------
= Introduction =
-------------------------
RobinViz (Reliability Oriented Bioinformatic Networks Visualization) is a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network visualization system designed to visually aid the prediction and verification processes of such networks. Embedding both the reliability (confirmation) values associated with the interactions and the verification data pertaining to them within a visualization model is a novel feature of the system. RobinViz is a free, open-source software protected under GPL. It is written in C++ and Python, and consists of almost 30,000 lines of code, excluding the employed libraries. 

Executable binaries of the system can be accessed via the Downloads link. These binaries can be downloaded and executed directly without any problems on most of the systems. Additionally we provide the source code implementations of the system. If the user wants to compile the source code and prepare her own executables we provide the necessary instructions under the Installation link of this Wiki. We next introduce the main GUI features and provide snapshots of a sample run. 

-------------------------
= Precautions =
-------------------------
During the wizard execution, the program may seem to be frozen when you click on the Next button. This means the program is downloading data, extracting an archive, or processing data. Please be patient until this process ends. You may follow the debug logs on the console.
-------------------------
= Graphical User Interface(GUI) =
-------------------------

== Menu ==

The Robinviz menu is simple. We have three menu tabs; File, View and Help.

From the *File* menu, you can execute(Ctrl+X), save(Ctrl+S) and load(Ctrl+O) sessions, display last execution(Ctrl+D) and update(Ctrl+U) Robinviz.

From the *View* menu, you can view color legend, clear view, pass to full screen, go to a desired peripheral view and refresh views.

From the *Help* menu, you can, while in Robinviz, access these manual pages and see the developer information.

== Visualizations and Tabs ==

=== Central Visualizations ===

We now introduce the GUI of Robinviz. All screenshots were taken with the *svn version 320*.

If you double click on "robinviz.exe" in windows or run the command "./robinviz.exe", you shall see the following empty screen.

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/1_first_time_opening.png||
|| When you open robinviz first time, you see this blank view ||

To start the visualizations, click *"File>Execute(Ctrl+X)"* from the File menu. 
Upon execution first-time users will be given the option to download
necessary raw data from online databases. Once the downloads are finished 
user will be provided with a series of dialogue boxes where all the parameters
of the visualization are determined by the user. For the following runs of RobinViz there will be more options 
to start a visualization. User may choose to view the last session or previously
saved sessions by clicking omn the appropriate options at the File menu. 
In either case you shall see snapshot similar to the one below. 

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/2_after_execution.png||
|| Snapshot after Execute or Load session operation with Central View||


====Central View====

You now have graph at the center where we call "Central View" and search box;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_2_after_clicks.png

Robinviz has 16 empty screen views where we call them as "Peripheral Views", around the "Central View" and a three tabbed search box. Using the search box, you can click and see "Central View" nodes and their labels from while "Cat" is on clicked. You can also query for proteins and observe the categories, that have the query protein, while "Pro" is on clicked. 

|| http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/4_2_category_search_box.png || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/3_2_protein_search_box.png ||
|| Search Box for Central View Labels ||  Search Box for proteins ||

Next, at the previous screenshot, you see the empty 16 screens. These screens are interactive and respond when you click on nodes(Categories,Biclusters) in "Central View". At each clicking on nodes, you shall see that a new graph appears at these empty screens. When you click 16 different nodes, you should obtain a similar snapshot;

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_after_clicks.png ||
|| When you fill 16 peripheral screens. ||

We call all these 16 views as "Peripheral Views";

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_1_after_clicks.png

"Peripheral Views" are the visualizations where you see the Protein-Protein Interaction sub-network created via proteins of the clicked category node.


====Gene Ontology(GO) Table====

In Robinviz we have also, some supporting tables and visualizations. Since we process over Gene Ontology categories, we form a table where we show each genes/proteins belongs to which categories as well. The following screen shows this table;

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/6_go_view.png ||
|| GO Table when you right click on nodes and select "Go Table" or when you right click anywhere of "Peripheral View" and again select "Go Table"||

If you right click on "Central View", you are allowed to see several other options. You may open the view in a new window for clear visibility, *print the visualization*, *save the graph of visualization in GML format* and *see the graph in another layout*. For example, if you try "Spring Embedder on Circular Tracks" for "Central View", the layout changes with nice animation.

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/7_run_layout.png ||
|| Sample demonstration of "Spring Embedder on Circular Tracks" for "Central View" ||

We should now be comfortable with main visualization screen. We now show how peripheral visualizations works.

=== Peripheral Visualizations ===

For "Peripheral Views" and their visualizations, we have new options and inherited options from "Central View". In "Peripheral Views", you now see proteins. We mention that you can click on nodes inside "Central View" and each nodes appears as a peripheral view around the "Central View". When you *right click* over
the first peripheral view and select *"Open in a new Window"*. Robinviz creates another window and show larger snapshot of clicked peripheral view.

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/8_open_peripherals.png ||
|| A peripheral view opened with a new window ||

Similarly, you can change layouts in that windows as well. For example, if you run "Spring Embedder on Circular Tracks", you will have,

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/8_open_peripherals_spring.png ||
|| A peripheral view after "Spring Embedder"||

You are allowed to open any peripheral views with a new window. In "Peripheral View", we have also one more option that you can do just using mouse clicks. Each protein nodes in "Peripheral View" allows you to right click on it and shows a pop up menu.
In that pop up menu, you have two options; "Get Information about the selected protein from Biogrid website", "See original sub network with one hop neighborhood" and "two hop neighborhood. If you select to see "Two hop neighborhood" you will see a new window,

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/9_protein_screen_1.png

and you complete three level views of Robinviz and the snapshot is as follows;

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/10_three_level_view.png ||
|| Central View at the background, a peripheral view on the left, a clicked node from peripheral view and its two hop neighborhood at the right ||

We told that you can change any view into any supported layouts. For demonstration, we apply different layout algorithms for all 16 peripherals and central view.

The snapshot is;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/11_change_layouts.png

-------------------------
= Sample Input Creation =
-------------------------

Hence our methodology works on the desired input requests, at this section, we provide how to create an input and make it meaningful for Robinviz. Since Robinviz has Wizard style Input menu, it is easy to follow step by step requests. In the paper, we mention two concepts of methodology to follow; *"Co-Expression"* and *"Co-Ontology"*. 

When you start the Execution Wizard from File->Execute, Data Manager might show up. Make sure that all of the sources are downloaded if you want to perform a manual-configuration run (this is not required for pre-configuration runs). Just click on the Download All button at the top right of the screen.

|| Data Manager ||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/data_manager.png ||

-------------------------
== Co-Ontology ==

Co-Ontology requires the selection of Protein-Protein Interaction Network, Coloring Methodology, Gene Ontology Category Selection and Association File Selection for GO category genes(We do all jobs under the existence of Biogrid id at each selections).

For easy understanding step by step input submission for Co-Ontology is as follows;

|| 0 ||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/0_starting_options1.png ||

|| First you must select among three starting options. Among these, please select *Define your manual settings* option to continue with PPI wizard. ||

|| 1 ||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/1_ppi_selection.png ||

|| First Select PPI data from Biogrid data from tree view. You are available to select multiple organisms. The tree view organized organism name and experimental methodology(see http://wiki.thebiogrid.org/doku.php/experimental_systems). For this setup, we select Homo Sapiens and all its experiments. Note also that this screen is *must select* screen for both Co-Ontology and Co-Expression. Please press Next button to continue and wait while PPI sources you selected are merged. ||

|| 2 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/2_select_concept.png ||

|| This wizard step allows you to select Co-Expression or Co-Ontology. We select Co-Ontology since we are going over at its path. To continue, please press Next button||

|| 3 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/3_color_assignment.png  ||

|| This screen allows you to select how all layouts in Robinviz should be colored. For details about the coloring see the paper. We select molecular Function at this step. Then, please press Next button  ||

|| 4 ||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/4_category_selection.png||

|| This screen is only for Co-Ontology. You must select at least one category among three main paths; Molecular Function, Cellular Component, Biological Process. We select several from each of these three main categorization. Please press Next button ||

|| 5 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_go_selection.png ||

|| Since we require genes/proteins from GO categorization, we download GO associations, we extract genes from these associations and convert to Biogrid id. For this case we select Filtered>Homo Sapiens. Finally, please press Finish button. This may take a long time (~10-15 min) as association sources will be downloaded, converted to Biogrid format. This is a first-run operation and following runs will be much more quicker. After the conversion, association files will be merged. You can track the process from the console window. ||

Then, for your patience Robinviz works for a while. During the execution the top of Robinviz window should be;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/6_note.png

Eventually, you will have following snapshot;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/7_result_self.png

With some clicks on *Central Nodes*, obtain the following

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/7_result.png

== Co-Expression ==

Co-Expression requires the selection of Protein-Protein Interaction Network, Coloring Methodology, Association File Selection for GO category genes(We do all jobs under the existence of Biogrid id at each selections), GEO File, Node weigh selection.

For easy understanding step by step input submission for Co-Expression is as follows;


|| 0 ||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/0_starting_options1.png ||

|| First you must select your options as we do in Co-Ontology. Please select *Define your manual settings* option to continue with PPI wizard. ||

|| 1 ||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/1_ppi_selection_2.png ||

|| First Select PPI data from Biogrid data from tree view. You are available to select multiple organisms. The tree view organized organism name and experimental methodology(see http://wiki.thebiogrid.org/doku.php/experimental_systems). For this setup, we select Saccharomyces Cerevisiae and all its experiments. Note also that this screen is *must select* screen for both Co-Ontology and Co-Expression. Please press Next button to continue. ||

|| 2 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/2_select_concept.png ||

|| This wizard step allows you to select Co-Expression or Co-Ontology. This time, we select Co-Expression since we are going over at its path. To continue, please press Next button||

|| 3 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/3_color_assignment.png  ||

|| This screen allows you to select how all layouts in Robinviz should be colored. For details about the coloring see the paper. We select molecular Function at this step. Then, please press Next button  ||

|| 4 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/4_assoc_selection.png ||

|| Since we require genes/proteins from GO categorization, we download GO associations, we extract genes from these associations and convert to Biogrid id. For this case we select Filtered>Saccharomyces Cerevisiae. After that, please press Next button ||

|| 5 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_select_bic.png ||

|| This wizard tab is unique for Co-Expression. You can select a biclustering algorithm among three named CC(Cheng and Church), Bimax(Prelic et al) and REAL(Erten and Sozdinler). For this run, we select CC and set parameters as shown in the figure above. Then, please continue with Next button.  ||


|| 6 || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/6_select_nodeweight.png ||

|| Node weights are importan clue for the co-expression execution. You can select three options as shown in the figure. For details refer to our conference paper. For this case, we select H-value. This is last wizard step for Co-Expression. Please press the Finish button to finalize input submission. ||

Then, for your patience Robinviz works for a while. During the execution the top of Robinviz window should be;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/6_note.png

Eventually, you will have following snapshot;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/7_result_2_remove_ratio_0_0.png

See that the graph might have so many edges, where we present a simple solution to see weighted edges. You can use *Remove Ratio*. For the above execution, *Remove Ratio* is 0.0. When you increase *Remove Ratio* to 0.2, you will obtain,

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/7_result_2_remove_ratio_0_2.png

where it is still confusing. When you change *Remove Ratio* to 0.6, with some clicks on *Central Nodes*, you will obtain the following figure;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/7_result_2_remove_ratio_0_6.png

where the abstract of visualization is more visible where you will see more weighted edges better.
